outputs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production asset: ONE transparent RGBA modular floor-marking SPRITE ATLAS for a strictly overhead, non-pixel 2D industrial horror game. Square canvas, preferably 2048x2048, arranged as an exact 4-column by 4-row grid of 16 equally sized cells, with equal generous transparent separation. Draw exactly ONE separate white-painted marking centered in EACH cell. There is NO visible grid, NO cell borders, NO lettering, NO numbers, NO background. All unpainted areas, small chips and gaps are genuine transparency. Paint hue is neutral pure WHITE, so game software can multiply any tint into it. Surface character comes mainly from alpha: matte rolled/stencilled industrial floor paint, fine uneven coverage, tiny transparent pinholes, a few modest scrapes and lightly irregular edges. Keep most paint opaque and silhouettes fully legible. No large missing chunks or disconnected broken pieces. No gray/black outline, no cast shadow, no glow, no 3D bevel, no photographic floor underneath. No perspective: every marking is flat and faces directly upward toward the camera. Clean consistent human-designed geometry with organic paint texture, never pixel art, never glossy plastic.
GEOMETRY AND MODULE ORDER, read rows left to right, top to bottom:
Row 1: (1) THIN straight horizontal line; (2) THIN square 90-degree L junction with arms pointing UP and RIGHT; (3) THIN T junction with arms pointing LEFT, RIGHT and UP; (4) THIN plus-shaped four-way cross.
Row 2: (5) THICK straight horizontal line; (6) THICK square 90-degree L junction with arms pointing UP and RIGHT; (7) THICK T junction with arms pointing LEFT, RIGHT and UP; (8) THICK plus-shaped cross.
Row 3: (9) bold directional arrow pointing UP with triangular arrowhead and straight shaft; (10) bold right-angle directional arrow, entering from the LEFT, turning 90 degrees UP and ending in an upward arrowhead; (11) horizontal double-headed arrow pointing LEFT and RIGHT; (12) standalone upward chevron, an inverted V with no shaft.
Row 4: (13) THREE aligned THIN horizontal rectangular dashes; (14) THREE aligned THICK horizontal rectangular dashes; (15) THIN horizontal line with a rounded closed LEFT end and a square flat RIGHT end; (16) THICK horizontal line with a rounded closed LEFT end and square flat RIGHT end.
MODULAR FIT: In rows 1 and 2 all junctions share the same exact geometric center and equal arm reach; ends finish flat and square at matching distance from cell center. Straight lines span the same width as T and cross junctions. Every line in row 1 has the same thin stroke width, roughly 6% of cell width; every line in row 2 has the same thick width, roughly 12% of cell width. Markings span roughly 70% of their cell width/height, with at least 12% transparent inset on all four sides. Do not join markings between cells. Render only these 16 separate white textured paint shapes on actual transparent alpha, with no additional marks or decorative presentation elements.

Edit this 4x4 sprite atlas into usable industrial PAINT DECALS. Keep the same sixteen symbols, the same row/column order and a real transparent background. Critical correction: REMOVE ALL white splatter, white dust, haze, detached paint fragments, brush smears and grunge OUTSIDE the sixteen actual symbol silhouettes. There must be completely transparent generous clean space around every symbol, and no marks between cells. REMOVE ALL gray outlines, inner rectangular borders, dark strokes, gray shading, embossed or sticker-like edge effects. The visible paint pixels must be neutral white only; texture is variable alpha, never gray shading. These are matte flat paint on a floor, NOT stickers, NOT tape, NOT raised objects. Within the white paint silhouettes add a restrained amount of small genuinely transparent pinholes and short fine worn streaks, with slightly irregular painted edges. Make transparent holes visibly reveal the empty background, not gray ink. Keep approximately 85-95 percent paint coverage so all geometry stays legible. The texture should feel like a few years of mild foot traffic, not ruined or peeling paint. Use consistent paint grain across all symbols. Keep shapes crisp, regular and exactly orthographic. Make thin row strokes 6 percent of the cell width and thick row strokes 12 percent; no extra border. Align all row 1 and row 2 flat arm endpoints to the same horizontal/vertical socket positions in each cell. L junction elbows and T junction intersections should be at their cell center so arms can connect to straight segments on a grid. Keep all sixteen shapes safely within their own equal 4x4 grid cells. Only the sixteen white paint shapes; no text, backgrounds, grid, shadows, frame or extra symbols.

reason: Extra paint splatter outside silhouettes, sticker-like outlines and inconsistent connector centers. Kept only as generation provenance; production uses generated paint coverage with deterministic module geometry.
